analysis:
The PR changes one line in docs/architecture/inference.md (line 2126, the `stop` row of the sampling-parameters table). It documents that Gemma 4 and `<think>` parsers exclude reasoning and tool-call spans from stop-string matching per request (`ReasoningStopScope`), and that the native block engine (diffusion Gemma) matches the whole output with no scope. This is documentation only: no code, keys, wire contract, cache identity or authorization changes. I examined the surrounding text in units 22 and 23 (lines 2026-2836) and found nothing else in the diff.

Threat-model relevance: the change describes request-scoped output handling inside the provider (TB-007, T-007). It does not touch the coordinator-to-provider WebSocket encryption (T-008), attestation (TB-009, TB-011), the prefix cache (T-041), or the fan helper. The surrounding text states that the sampler and stop handling are not part of prompt or cache identity, so SSD cache scope, HMAC lookup tags and TTL are unaffected. The documented behavior is a correctness and semantics detail, not a new trust boundary or disclosure path.

Unverified contract: I could not check that the `ReasoningStopScope` implementation matches this description, because no source was supplied. This is a documentation-accuracy question only. Stop strings are a consumer-supplied request field and, per the doc, act only on held-back detokenised text. No security regression or threat-model gap is identified.
